🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Now let me also verify the perf test passes here and check `dart analyze` on touched files. Also run the ansi_markdown tests to make sure byte-parity claims hold.

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. callers/callees of changed symbols,

impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. - **PR #**: 1502
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1502
- **Title**: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1496-wrap-ansi-line-perf` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +378
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1502
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1502
- **Title**: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1496-wrap-ansi-line-perf` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +378
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|

# pr-1502: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits

## Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere

  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via

🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1502
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1502
- **Title**: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1496-wrap-ansi-line-perf` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +378
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1502
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1502
- **Title**: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1496-wrap-ansi-line-perf` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +378
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Now I need to verify the claimed equivalence. Key concerns:

1. **Old tokenizer regex** `r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.'` with unicode:true. `.` matches any code point (with unicode flag, also handles surrogates? In Dart, RegExp with unicode: true, `.` matches a code point — surrogates handled as pairs). Old loop:
   - `token == '` → flushWord, boundary space handling.
   - else: `wordTokens.add(token)`; `if (!token.startsWith('\x1b')) wordVisible += _tokenWidth(token)`.
   
   Wait — old code treats space specially only if token is exactly '. In new code, `u == 0x20` checks the code unit. What about non-breaking space (U+00A0)? Old regex `.` would match it as a visible rune; `_tokenWidth` — token length 1, unit 0xA0 >= 0x80, so falls to `tuiTextWidth(token)`. `tuiTextWidth` measures grapheme width — likely 1 for NBSP. New code: NBSP code unit 0xA0, not 0x20, so goes to rune classification: `tuiRuneCellWidth(0xA0)` → rune < 0x80? No (0xA0 ≥ 0x80). `_isZeroWidth(0xA0)`? probably false. `_isWide`? false → width 1. Same.

   But is `tuiTextWidth` for a single-rune string always equal to `tuiRuneCellWidth(rune)`? For a lone surrogate pair rune... yes. What about control characters? E.g. tab character U+0009: old code `_tokenWidth`: token.length == 1, unit 0x09 < 0x20 → width 0. New: `tuiRuneCellWidth(0x09)` → rune < 0x20 → 0. Same. The PR description mentions tab in the adversarial alphabet — OK.

   **A subtle divergence**: `_tokenWidth` fast path only when token.length == 1; for length>1 non-ESC tokens it calls `tuiTextWidth(token)` which does grapheme segmentation. Old tokenizer emits one token per rune (`.`, unicode) so tokens are always single runes. OK equivalent.

🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Now let me also verify the perf test passes here and check `dart analyze` on touched files. Also run the ansi_markdown tests to make sure byte-parity claims hold.

On a heavily loaded shared runner, JIT could be 5-10× slower — ASCII test at 16.7ms local could hit ~100-170ms on a bad day. Known concern, mitigations mentioned. SUGGESTION: consider tagging/skipping absolute-budget tests under a stress flag. Also the test file runs 1M-cell wraps ~7+ times × warm-up — with slow CI this adds seconds to the default suite. SUGGESTION.

5. **Public API behavior change: views are now live aliases.** `formattedLines`/`wrappedRows`/`lineStartRows` getters now return lists that (a) grow in place across syncs, and (b) shrink via `_rollbackGrownTail` truncation. Previously each sync returned a fresh snapshot (spread copies). The TUI consumer (`_WrapCache`) uses it synchronously per frame and overwrites `cache.rows` after each sync, so it's safe today. # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1502
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1502
- **Title**: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1496-wrap-ansi-line-perf` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +378
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

# pr-1502: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits

## Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).

  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere

🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1502
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1502
- **Title**: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `fix/1496-wrap-ansi-line-perf` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 3
- **Additions**: +378
- **Deletions**: -77
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T16:11:07Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T16:28:17Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`

🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Now let me also verify the perf test passes here and check `dart analyze` on touched files. Also run the ansi_markdown tests to make sure byte-parity claims hold.

1. **Formatting churn in MarkdownSurface.render / _renderWhole / resolveMarkdownSurface** — pure `dart format` reformatting, unrelated to perf fix. Minor scope creep. On a heavily loaded shared runner, JIT could be 5-10× slower — ASCII test at 16.7ms local could hit ~100-170ms on a bad day. Known concern, mitigations mentioned. SUGGESTION: consider tagging/skipping absolute-budget tests under a stress flag. Also the test file runs 1M-cell wraps ~7+ times × warm-up — with slow CI this adds seconds to the default suite. SUGGESTION.

5. **Public API behavior change: views are now live aliases.** `formattedLines`/`wrappedRows`/`lineStartRows` getters now return lists that (a) grow in place across syncs, and (b) shrink via `_rollbackGrownTail` truncation. Previously each sync returned a fresh snapshot (spread copies). Any consumer holding a view across syncs sees its content change — and worse, `identical(view1, view2)` may now be true across syncs where content changed. The TUI consumer (`_WrapCache`) uses it synchronously per frame and overwrites `cache.rows` after each sync, so it's safe today. But the public getters' doc comments don't state the liveness contract. IMPORTANT (API contract change, undocumented) or SUGGESTION. I'll say IMPORTANT... hmm. # pr-1502: perf(1496): single-pass wrapAnsiLine batching + O(delta) transcript commits

## Description

Fixes #1496

## Root cause (per repro, not the cache-bandaid shape)

The profile's `(84 calls, mean 12.9s)` decomposes into two real costs, both reproduced locally:

1. **wrapAnsiLine paid per visible cell**: the hoisted per-char regex tokenizer (`RegExp(r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.', unicode: true)`) matched + allocated a `String` + classified width for EVERY rune, and `flushWord` re-measured every token a second time. Linear per call, but a ~100ns/cell constant — transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines, so each committed/throttled re-render paid it whole.
2. **TranscriptMarkdown._commitTo rebuilt the accumulated arrays per sync**: `[..._formatted]` / `[..._rows]` / `[..._starts]` spread-copies of everything committed so far, on every flush — O(total) per sync, O(total²) per session.

## Fix (algorithmic, public API and output byte-identical)

- `wrapAnsiLine` now scans code units directly and batches maximal **same-width rune runs** into single tokens (`_WrapPart`: one substring, one carried width). The SGR state machine, word/hard-cut rules, close positions and boundary-space drops are carried over verbatim; SGR matching is the exact `ESC [ [0-9;]* m` shape; surrogate pairs and lone-ESC quirks preserved. New `tuiRuneCellWidth()` classifies a rune without building a 1-char string (same tables as `tuiGraphemeWidth`). The fitting-line early-out is untouched.
- `_commitTo` appends to the durable caches **in place** (same pattern as the existing `_rollbackGrownTail`); `_expose` still republishes fresh views every sync, so no stale alias is served.

## Equivalence proof (goldens untouched)

- **349,520 exhaustive differential cases** (16-symbol adversarial alphabet: SGR set/reset, lone ESC, `[ m ; 0` meta-chars, wide ✅/中, zero-width combining/ZWJ, surrogate-pair 𐐀, tab × sequence lengths ≤ 4 × widths 1..5): byte-identical pre/post. This caught one real subtlety — a zero-width rune after an overflowing wide rune must still close the row (`col + 0 > width` is possible once `col > width`).
- 126-row randomized corpus (prose/styled/CJK/one-word × 6 sizes × 5 widths + 3 stepped transcript sessions): identical.
- Repo suites green: ansi_markdown (wrap semantics), transcript_markdown_perf (adversarial incremental≡one-shot byte parity), transcript_table_render, viewport-fold golden, composer-wrap goldens, markdown_surface, inline_markdown — 184 targeted tests, zero golden churn. `dart analyze` clean on touched files; full `test/cli` run shows only the host's known `openpty`/network-download failures (verified identical on the clean baseline).

## Numbers (before → after, median of 5, warm VM, local arm64)

wrapAnsiLine @ 1M visible cells — acceptance bar < 100ms, all shapes now under it:

| shape | before | after | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| ASCII prose | 116.6 ms | **16.7 ms** | 7.0× |
| single word (hard-cut) | 106.3 ms | **5.4 ms** | 19.7× |
| SGR-styled prose | 81.4 ms | **30.0 ms** | 2.7× |
| CJK prose | 164.0 ms | **85.2 ms** | 1.9× |

Growth stays linear (10K/100K/1M = 0.3/1.6/16.7 ms prose). TranscriptMarkdown session of 84 syncs to 100,807 lines / 108,244 rows: per-sync cost no longer grows with the transcript — **4→7 ms before (O(total) copies) vs flat 1–3 ms after (O(delta))**.

## Regression guard

`test/cli/wrap_ansi_line_perf_test.dart` (runs in the default suite, ~0.5s): 1M-cell absolute budgets (<100 ms median, 6–19× local headroom per the gh-1357 bound-sitting lesson) + 2×-input growth-shape contracts (≤3.2×; quadratic would measure ~4×) over the prose, CJK and hard-cut paths, plus a scale correctness anchor (width respected, reassembly invariant).

## Remaining (not in scope here)

- CJK/styled constants could drop further (rune-table binary search, SGR-run batching); the growth contracts will hold them to linear.
- `_expose` still copies views on open-table tails (small, bounded by table size).
