# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold

  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Now I need to verify the claimed equivalence. Key concerns:

1. **Old tokenizer regex** `r'\x1b\[[0-9;]*m|.'` with unicode:true. `.` matches any code point (with unicode flag, also handles surrogates? In Dart, RegExp with unicode: true, `.` matches a code point — surrogates handled as pairs). Old loop:
   - `token == '` → flushWord, boundary space handling.
   - else: `wordTokens.add(token)`; `if (!token.startsWith('\x1b')) wordVisible += _tokenWidth(token)`.
   
   Wait — old code treats space specially only if token is exactly '. In new code, `u == 0x20` checks the code unit. What about non-breaking space (U+00A0)? Old regex `.` would match it as a visible rune; `_tokenWidth` — token length 1, unit 0xA0 >= 0x80, so falls to `tuiTextWidth(token)`. `tuiTextWidth` measures grapheme width — likely 1 for NBSP. New code: NBSP code unit 0xA0, not 0x20, so goes to rune classification: `tuiRuneCellWidth(0xA0)` → rune < 0x80? No (0xA0 ≥ 0x80). `_isZeroWidth(0xA0)`? probably false. `_isWide`? false → width 1. Same.

   But is `tuiTextWidth` for a single-rune string always equal to `tuiRuneCellWidth(rune)`? For a lone surrogate pair rune... yes. What about control characters? E.g. tab character U+0009: old code `_tokenWidth`: token.length == 1, unit 0x09 < 0x20 → width 0. New: `tuiRuneCellWidth(0x09)` → rune < 0x20 → 0. Same. The PR description mentions tab in the adversarial alphabet — OK.

   **A subtle divergence**: `_tokenWidth` fast path only when token.length == 1; for length>1 non-ESC tokens it calls `tuiTextWidth(token)` which does grapheme segmentation. Old tokenizer emits one token per rune (`.`, unicode) so tokens are always single runes. OK equivalent.

2. **Zero-width rune close check**: Old hard-cut path: `if (col > 0 && !token.startsWith('\x1b') && col + tokenWidth > width) closeRow();` For a zero-width token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] + 0 > width` requires `col > width`. New code: `if (col > width) closeRow();` — old also had `col > 0` guard, but if col > width then col > 0 anyway (col is ≥0; width ≥1 typically; can width be 0? wrapAnsiLine with width=0? Hmm — if width == 0, old: col=0, tokenWidth≥... let's check width==0 with zero-width token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] false initially; writeToken; then next zero-width token: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] still → no close. New: `col > width` = `0 > 0` false. Same. For w>0 hard-cut with width 0: new `cap = col == 0 ? (w > 0? width~/w = 0)` → cap <= 0 → `continue` — infinite loop? Wait: `while (from < part.runes)`: `if (col > 0 && ...)` col is 0; `cap = col == 0 ? (w > width ? 1 : width ~/ w)` — if w > width (w≥1 > 0) → cap = 1. OK not infinite. If w == width... w > width false when w=... width=0, w≥1>0 → cap=1. OK fine. But what if width ≤ 0 and w == width can't happen since w ≥ 1 and width 0... fine.

   Actually wait — infinite loop risk: `if (cap <= 0) continue;` — after `closeRow()`, col = 0, so next iteration computes `cap = col == 0 ? ...` = `w > width ? 1 : width ~/ w`. When can `cap <= 0` occur after closeRow? col==0 path: if w > width → 1, else width~/w ≥ 1 (since w ≤ width). So cap ≥ 1 always. The `cap <= 0` guard is when col > 0 path: `(width - col) ~/ w` — but we closed row when `col > 0 && col + w > width`, i.e., col > width - w, so width - col < w → `~/ w` = 0... wait but after closeRow() col becomes 0 in the same iteration, then cap computed with col==0 → ≥1. Hmm, but the cap is computed AFTER closeRow in the same loop iteration. Sequence: `if (col > 0 && col + w > width) closeRow();` then `cap = col == 0 ? ... : (width-col)~/w`. Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Given in-tree consumers are safe, SUGGESTION might be more appropriate per the anti-pattern of over-requesting changes. I'll go with SUGGESTION for doc contract, since no actual breakage exists.

Hmm, let me reconsider the CJK quadratic severity once more. Measured: 4× input → ~14-18× time on the CJK hard-cut path. The PR's own framing: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines" and old code was ~164ms/1M CJK cells. New code for a 100KB CJK line (50K runes, no spaces): ~120ms — comparable to old. For 500KB: ~3s vs old ~800ms — regression. For 2MB: ~45-50s vs old ~3s — severe. This path is reachable in real transcripts (pasted minified content is usually ASCII; CJK unbroken 500KB+ is rarer, but emoji/base64... base64 is ASCII → O(1) path; long emoji runs → surrogate pairs, same quadratic). A 100KB base64 line hard-cuts fine (ASCII). The realistic exposure is long unbroken non-ASCII (CJK/emoji) tokens ≥ ~100KB. Also note the old code was O(n) here; the PR made it O(n²) — a regression the PR's regression tests can't see (CJK test words are short, ASCII test covers only the ascii fast path). For a perf PR whose acceptance criteria is linearity, shipping a hidden quadratic on the path it rewrote is a significant finding. I'll rate IMPORTANT (not BLOCKING — it's perf, not correctness; the verdict table reserves BLOCKING for correctness/bug/security/CI).

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

SUGGESTION.

The TUI consumer (`_WrapCache`) uses it synchronously per frame and overwrites `cache.rows` after each sync, so it's safe today. 🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Consumers are internal (fa_tui_viewport, fa_tui) — both use views synchronously per frame and overwrite cache references after each sync, so the live-alias change is safe in-tree today. Given in-tree consumers are safe, SUGGESTION might be more appropriate per the anti-pattern of over-requesting changes. I'll go with SUGGESTION for doc contract, since no actual breakage exists.

Hmm, let me reconsider the CJK quadratic severity once more. Measured: 4× input → ~14-18× time on the CJK hard-cut path. The PR's own framing: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines" and old code was ~164ms/1M CJK cells. New code for a 100KB CJK line (50K runes, no spaces): ~120ms — comparable to old. For 500KB: ~3s vs old ~800ms — regression. For 2MB: ~45-50s vs old ~3s — severe. This path is reachable in real transcripts (pasted minified content is usually ASCII; CJK unbroken 500KB+ is rarer, but emoji/base64... base64 is ASCII → O(1) path; long emoji runs → surrogate pairs, same quadratic). A 100KB base64 line hard-cuts fine (ASCII). The realistic exposure is long unbroken non-ASCII (CJK/emoji) tokens ≥ ~100KB. Also note the old code was O(n) here; the PR made it O(n²) — a regression the PR's regression tests can't see (CJK test words are short, ASCII test covers only the ascii fast path). For a perf PR whose acceptance criteria is linearity, shipping a hidden quadratic on the path it rewrote is a significant finding. I'll rate IMPORTANT (not BLOCKING — it's perf, not correctness; the verdict table reserves BLOCKING for correctness/bug/security/CI).

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Consumers are internal (fa_tui_viewport, fa_tui) — both use views synchronously per frame and overwrite cache references after each sync, so the live-alias change is safe in-tree today. But it's still a latent contract change; and `_rollbackGrownTail` truncation shrinking a list a caller may hold is a real behavioral hazard for future consumers. I'll rate this IMPORTANT (document the liveness contract on the getters) — or SUGGESTION? The instructions: IMPORTANT = real maintainability/correctness issue. Undocumented aliasing of a public-API list that mutates and even shrinks between calls — I'll say IMPORTANT, fix = one doc-comment sentence. Actually the getters are on a class only used internally... but the class is public (no underscore) and `wrapAnsiLine` is public API too. Given in-tree consumers are safe, SUGGESTION might be more appropriate per the anti-pattern of over-requesting changes. I'll go with SUGGESTION for doc contract, since no actual breakage exists.

Hmm, let me reconsider the CJK quadratic severity once more. Measured: 4× input → ~14-18× time on the CJK hard-cut path. The PR's own framing: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines" and old code was ~164ms/1M CJK cells. New code for a 100KB CJK line (50K runes, no spaces): ~120ms — comparable to old. For 500KB: ~3s vs old ~800ms — regression. For 2MB: ~45-50s vs old ~3s — severe. This path is reachable in real transcripts (pasted minified content is usually ASCII; CJK unbroken 500KB+ is rarer, but emoji/base64... base64 is ASCII → O(1) path; long emoji runs → surrogate pairs, same quadratic). A 100KB base64 line hard-cuts fine (ASCII). The realistic exposure is long unbroken non-ASCII (CJK/emoji) tokens ≥ ~100KB. Also note the old code was O(n) here; the PR made it O(n²) — a regression the PR's regression tests can't see (CJK test words are short, ASCII test covers only the ascii fast path). For a perf PR whose acceptance criteria is linearity, shipping a hidden quadratic on the path it rewrote is a significant finding. I'll rate IMPORTANT (not BLOCKING — it's perf, not correctness; the verdict table reserves BLOCKING for correctness/bug/security/CI).

Wait — also consider: does the wide-rune classification for the perf test's CJK growth test exercise partOffset at all? cjkProse words are ≤17 runes (34 cells < 80) so no hard-cut. Confirmed gap.

Other smaller findings:

1. **Unrelated formatting churn** (`MarkdownSurface.render`, `_renderWhole`, `resolveMarkdownSurface`, stray blank line) — SUGGESTION: keep the diff scoped; the reformat also suggests a formatter version drift that could churn other files.

2. **Perf-test absolute budgets in the default suite** — SUGGESTION: risk of flake on loaded CI (100ms budget, 16.7ms local median = ~6× headroom; slow JIT-on-shared-runner could exceed). The gh-1357 lesson is cited. Optionally gate absolute budgets behind a non-default tag. I'll mention briefly as SUGGESTION.

3. `writeRunSliced`'s `if (cap <= 0) continue;` — unreachable dead guard (after closeRow, col==0 ⇒ cap ≥ 1). Could confuse readers; harmless. Could fold into the quadratic comment as SUGGESTION. Actually if cap <= 0 were ever hit it'd be an infinite loop — the guard protects against that but `continue` without advancing from would indeed infinite-loop if reached with col>0... it's not reachable. Skip or minor mention. I'll mention within the quadratic comment file as a note? Better keep comments focused. I might add it as a small SUGGESTION.

4. `partOffset` recomputation — part of the quadratic finding.

5. Check `_WrapPart.style` for lone ESC: `wordParts.add(_WrapPart.style('\x1b'))` — the old code `wordTokens.add(token)` where token='[REDACTED:Sensitive Value]'; flushWord non-hard-cut branch writes it via writeToken → row.write + activeSgr.add. 🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Now let me also verify the perf test passes here and check `dart analyze` on touched files. Also run the ansi_markdown tests to make sure byte-parity claims hold.

While that runs, let me do the exhaustive pass on remaining review items:

1. **Formatting churn in MarkdownSurface.render / _renderWhole / resolveMarkdownSurface** — pure `dart format` reformatting, unrelated to perf fix. Minor scope creep. Note: was this `dart format` output? The repo presumably enforces formatting. The reformatting looks like it resulted from a formatter version difference. SUGGESTION to keep unrelated hunks out.

2. **The stray blank line added** after the TranscriptMarkdown closing brace (line 1339 `+` before `/// How [MarkdownSurface.render]...`). Trivial; formatter artifact.

3. **`tuiRuneCellWidth` fast path** — `rune < 0x80` — covers C0 controls and DEL. Consistent with `_tokenWidth`'s old ASCII fast path. ✓

4. **Perf test absolute budgets** — flake risk on slow CI. 6× headroom on ASCII (16.7 vs 100). Hard-cut 5.4ms vs 100 = 18×. On a heavily loaded shared runner, JIT could be 5-10× slower — ASCII test at 16.7ms local could hit ~100-170ms on a bad day. Known concern, mitigations mentioned. SUGGESTION: consider tagging/skipping absolute-budget tests under a stress flag. Also the test file runs 1M-cell wraps ~7+ times × warm-up — with slow CI this adds seconds to the default suite. SUGGESTION.

5. **Public API behavior change: views are now live aliases.** `formattedLines`/`wrappedRows`/`lineStartRows` getters now return lists that (a) grow in place across syncs, and (b) shrink via `_rollbackGrownTail` truncation. Previously each sync returned a fresh snapshot (spread copies). Any consumer holding a view across syncs sees its content change — and worse, `identical(view1, view2)` may now be true across syncs where content changed. The TUI consumer (`_WrapCache`) uses it synchronously per frame and overwrites `cache.rows` after each sync, so it's safe today. But the public getters' doc comments don't state the liveness contract. IMPORTANT (API contract change, undocumented) or SUGGESTION. I'll say IMPORTANT... hmm. Actually let me double check `_publishCleanViews` pre-existed. Check git show origin/main version.

{"content":"💡 **SUGGESTION: document the live-view contract on the public getters**

With the in-place commit, the published views (`formattedLines` / `wrappedRows` / `lineStartRows` via `_publishCleanViews`) are now **aliases of the durable caches that grow in place on every sync — and shrink via `_rollbackGrownTail`'s `length =` truncation**. Before this change, `_commitTo` spread-copied, so every sync returned a fresh frozen snapshot and a caller could hold a view indefinitely.

The in-tree consumers (`_WrapCache` in fa_tui/fa_tui_viewport) are safe: they consume the views synchronously per frame and re-fetch after each `sync()`. But the contract changed silently, and a future caller that snapshots a view across syncs (or diffs two generations by list identity, which can now be `identical` while content grew) gets burned. One sentence on the three getters' doc comments — "returned lists are live views owned by this instance; do not hold across `sync()` calls" — pins the contract. Not blocking.

🎉 1 test passed.

Confirmed: CJK single-word hard-cut is quadratic — 4× input → ~14-18× time (16→21→79→292ms; doubling ratios 1.3, 3.8, 3.7 — roughly 4× per doubling, classic O(n²)). 80K CJK runes = 160KB line, still fast at 292ms. At 1M runes (2MB line) it would be ~45s! Compare old code: per-rune regex+measure at ~100ns/cell → 1M cells ≈ 100-160ms. So for long unbroken CJK words the new code is orders of magnitude SLOWER than the old code it replaced. The PR's own stated motivation: "transcript bursts are single multi-100KB lines". A 100KB CJK word = 50K runes ≈ 120ms — still OK-ish, but a 500KB CJK token (no spaces) = 250K runes ≈ 3s vs old ~40ms. This is a real regression on an adversarial-but-plausible input, and the added regression test does NOT cover it: `cjkProse` inserts a space every 17 runes so words are 34 cells < 80 width and never hard-cut; the hard-cut test is ASCII-only (O(1) offset path). The growth contracts pass while the CJK hard-cut path is quadratic.

Fix would be simple: since writeRunSliced slices sequentially with monotonically increasing `from`, compute unit offsets incrementally (track unit position) rather than re-walking from 0 — O(n) total.

Severity: The PR is a perf fix; this reintroduces a worse-than-before quadratic on a specific path the old code handled linearly. I'd call it IMPORTANT (arguably BLOCKING? It's a perf regression, not a correctness bug; per the verdict rules BLOCKING = correctness/bug/security/CI. A severe perf regression on plausible adversarial input in a perf PR... I'll classify IMPORTANT — the machine protocol wants blocking only for correctness/bugs. Hmm — but is it "broken behavior"? An attacker/agent outputting a 2MB unbroken CJK string would freeze the TUI for ~45s+, vs ~200ms before. That's arguably a regression of the exact behavior the PR fixes. But the old behavior before PR: regex tokenizer 164ms/1M cells — the freeze was 12.9s mean over 84 calls for real transcripts. I think IMPORTANT is right; it's a real maintainability/correctness issue worth fixing, but merge doesn't cause a bug for normal inputs. Given "when in doubt start one level higher" — I'll mark it IMPORTANT.)

Also check: surrogate-pair runes (astral plane, e.g. 𐐀) in hard-cut — partOffset walks pairs; same quadratic applies.

Now let me also verify the perf test passes here and check `dart analyze` on touched files. Also run the ansi_markdown tests to make sure byte-parity claims hold.

While that runs, let me do the exhaustive pass on remaining review items:

1. **Formatting churn in MarkdownSurface.render / _renderWhole / resolveMarkdownSurface** — pure `dart format` reformatting, unrelated to perf fix. Minor scope creep. Note: was this `dart format` output? The repo presumably enforces formatting. The reformatting looks like it resulted from a formatter version difference. SUGGESTION to keep unrelated hunks out.

2. **The stray blank line added** after the TranscriptMarkdown closing brace (line 1339 `+` before `/// How [MarkdownSurface.render]...`). Trivial; formatter artifact.

3. **`tuiRuneCellWidth` fast path** — `rune < 0x80` — covers C0 controls and DEL. Consistent with `_tokenWidth`'s old ASCII fast path. ✓

4. **Perf test absolute budgets** — flake risk on slow CI. 6× headroom on ASCII (16.7 vs 100). Hard-cut 5.4ms vs 100 = 18×. On a heavily loaded shared runner, JIT could be 5-10× slower — ASCII test at 16.7ms local could hit ~100-170ms on a bad day. Known concern, mitigations mentioned. SUGGESTION: consider tagging/skipping absolute-budget tests under a stress flag. Also the test file runs 1M-cell wraps ~7+ times × warm-up — with slow CI this adds seconds to the default suite. SUGGESTION.

5. **Public API behavior change: views are now live aliases.** `formattedLines`/`wrappedRows`/`lineStartRows` getters now return lists that (a) grow in place across syncs, and (b) shrink via `_rollbackGrownTail` truncation. Previously each sync returned a fresh snapshot (spread copies). Any consumer holding a view across syncs sees its content change — and worse, `identical(view1, view2)` may now be true across syncs where content changed. The TUI consumer (`_WrapCache`) uses it synchronously per frame and overwrites `cache.rows` after each sync, so it's safe today. But the public getters' doc comments don't state the liveness contract. IMPORTANT (API contract change, undocumented) or SUGGESTION. I'll say IMPORTANT... hmm.
